question: Does the HTTP fingerprint substrate SHA256(status||body_bytes||sorted_filtered_headers) retain discriminating same-status body-only (200 vs 200, body-only >0.5, status-only 0.0, full > status strictly, headers-no-CLEN 0.0, Content-Length varies) and header-only discrimination (200 vs 200, bodies identical, full 1.0 > max(status 0.0, body 0.0), Content-Length identical, headers-only 1.0) with null stability (FP<0.05, null 0.0, CI contains 0.0) and writable permission/session controls >=0.7 when moved from localhost Flask dev server (Werkzeug) to production WSGI (gunicorn) + nginx reverse proxy (emulating CDN header folding/ordering) and, where image available, BrowserGym/AgentLab substrate, under concurrency and distributed session replication where bootstrap CIs are tested for non-degeneracy?
hypothesis: The identical fingerprint hash(status_code || body_bytes || sorted_filtered_standard_headers) with EXCLUDED_HEADERS={Date,Server,X-Request-Id} (identical algorithm to EXP-RUNTIME-35749360317 and EXP-RUNTIME-35741906498 run_experiment.py:compute_fingerprint, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':')) will generalize from localhost Flask dev server (Werkzeug 3.1.8) to a production-like stack (Flask 3.1.3 + PyJWT 2.14.0 HS256 + SQLite WAL, served via gunicorn 22+ sync workers x2 + nginx 1.25+ reverse proxy on 127.0.0.1, with nginx proxy_set_header / header lowercasing/ordering/whitespace normalization) and retain deterministic discrimination: (H1) same-status body-only full-vector 1.0 >0.5 on A vs C (31B vs 117B distinct SHA, both 200, non-CLEN headers identical), body-only 1.0 >0.5 on A vs C and A vs B (70B), status-only 0.0, full > status strictly, headers-no-CLEN 0.0, Content-Length 31/70/117 varies ==body_len, null 0.0 FP<0.05; (H2) header-only full 1.0 and headers-only 1.0 with status 0.0 body 0.0 on A vs E (31B identical, CLEN 31 identical) and each isolated header (Cache-Control only, ETag only, Set-Cookie only) 1.0 with CLEN identity; (H3) writable permission escalation 403 vs 200 and session invalidation 401 vs 200 each full >=0.7 with nulls 0.0 on the same production stack across gunicorn workers (distributed session/role commit visible); (H4) concurrency (4 concurrent clients, 2 gunicorn workers via nginx round-robin, jitter 50-150ms) does not introduce false discrimination in null (null still 0.0, FP<0.05) and bootstrap CI non-degeneracy is measured: if fingerprints remain deterministic, CI will be degenerate [1.0,1.0]/[0.0,0.0] (declared deterministic, not precision), if nginx/gunicorn introduces header variance (e.g., Connection keep-alive vs close, Via, X-Request-Id excluded correctly), headers-no-CLEN must remain 0.0 on body-only and body-only 0.0 on header-only; (H5) realistic header folding/ordering/case (Cache-Control max-age=3600 with varied case/whitespace/order, multiple Set-Cookie if supported) is normalized by sorted lowercased aggregation so discrimination remains determined by logical header value not serialization. Failure of any mandatory H1-H3 isolation on the production stack falsifies production generalization; concurrency/header-folding outcomes are exploratory but high-information for freshness/delta-repair trust.
falsifier: Hypothesis falsified if, on the production WSGI+nginx stack with verified commits (SQLite SELECT before each batch, batch_state_log.jsonl) and status/header/body identity checks passing, any of: (a) same-status body-only A vs C full <=0.5 or body-only <=0.5 or status-only !=0.0 or full <= status (not strictly >) or headers-no-CLEN !=0.0 or Content-Length not varying (31/70/117 not distinct) or Content-Length != body_len or non-CLEN filtered headers not identical; (b) header-only A vs E full <=0.5 or headers-only <=0.5 or status-only !=0.0 or body-only !=0.0 or Content-Length not identical (31 !=31) or per-isolation Cache-Control/ETag/Set-Cookie !=1.0 on full/headers-only; (c) null stability violation: any production null resampling (body-A resampled N1, header-A resampled, 403 null, 401 null) full >0.05 or CI does not contain 0.0 or body/status on null !=0.0, including under concurrency; (d) writable permission-level (reader 200 vs admin 200 via same body A vs C, and classic 403 vs 200 via UPDATE users) or session invalidation (401 vs 200 via DELETE sessions) on production stack with cross-worker commit yields full <0.7 or null >0.05. Each is bounded falsification for the named branch on production WSGI+nginx. Infrastructure failure yields MEASUREMENT_INVALID not falsification: gunicorn/nginx binary unavailable, port bind failure, SQLite COMMIT not verified, status mismatch (non-200 where 200 required), body write not committed, fingerprint hash mismatch, nginx config parse error, BrowserGym image pull failure (then that substrate marked NOT_TESTED, gunicorn+nginx remains primary). MEASUREMENT_INVALID also if header folding test cannot be isolated because nginx strips/reorders filtered headers outside included set.

baselines.description: Fingerprint = status code only (hash(status)). Expected 0.0 on all same-status comparisons (200 vs 200) for body-only and header-only branches on production stack (proves status confound removed); expected 1.0 on permission escalation 403 vs 200 and session invalidation 401 vs 200. Fails isolation if >0 on 200 vs 200.

Fingerprint = response body SHA-256 only (hash(body_bytes)). Expected 1.0 deterministically on same-status body-only A vs C (117B vs 31B) and A vs B (70B vs 31B) where bodies differ, and 0.0 on body-only null and on header-only A vs E where bodies identical 31B SHA d0ca833f843c...; also 1.0 on classic 403/401 where bodies differ. Proves body carries signal when status constant.

Fingerprint = sorted filtered standard headers only (Cache-Control, ETag, Set-Cookie, Vary, Content-Type, Content-Length, Connection) excluding Date/Server/X-Request-Id. Expected on production stack: body-only branch 1.0 SOLELY via body-correlated Content-Length (31 vs 70 vs 117) with headers-no-CLEN 0.0; header-only branch 1.0 via Cache-Control/ETag/Set-Cookie variation with bodies identical. Null 0.0. Isolates body-correlated vs independent header signal.

Filtered headers minus Content-Length (same set minus Content-Length). Expected 0.0 on same-status body-only A vs C / A vs B on production stack (no independent header drift, all non-CLEN headers identical), and 1.0 on header-only A vs E and per-header isolations (Cache-Control only, ETag only, Set-Cookie only). Proves body-only signal not via independent header drift and header-only signal not via CLEN correlation.

positive_control: Production WSGI+nginx positive controls (primary): (P-BODY) same-status body-only via writable server-side body_config/content_variant on Flask 3.1.3 + PyJWT 2.14.0 HS256 + SQLite WAL served via gunicorn 2x sync workers + nginx reverse proxy (nginx proxy_pass to gunicorn upstream, proxy_set_header Host $host, proxy_http_version 1.1, proxy_set_header Connection ""). Three body states GET /resource authenticated (200 for all): STATE_A 31B {"data":"hello","version":1} SHA d0ca833f843c6d70ec9d6755f52a92dcbfc8b4ab601b871bced09ad027172e34, STATE_B ~70B {"data":"hello","items":["a","b"],"role":"reader","version":1} SHA 67c186f2cee..., STATE_C 117B {"admin_note":"sensitive:42","count":42,"data":"hello","items":["a","b","c"],"role":"admin","version":1} SHA b46c461cceee... (exact lengths logged, must satisfy 31<70<117 and CLEN==body_len). Non-CLEN headers held constant: Cache-Control max-age=3600, ETag W/"fixed-aaa-111", Vary Accept-Encoding, no Set-Cookie, Content-Type application/json. POST /admin/set_body_variant commits SQLite before 200, verified by SELECT. Primary A vs C must be full 1.0 >0.5, body-only 1.0, status 0.0, headers-no-CLEN 0.0. (P-HEADER) header-only via writable header_config on same stack: STATE_A same 31B body, STATE_E combined header variant (Cache-Control max-age=0,must-revalidate + ETag W/"changed-bbb-222" + Set-Cookie session=xyz + Vary Accept-Encoding,Origin) bodies identical 31B SHA same, CLEN 31 identical. Per-isolation: Cache-Control only, ETag only, Set-Cookie only each expected full 1.0 headers-only 1.0 status 0.0 body 0.0. (P-WRITABLE) classic permission 403 vs 200 (UPDATE users SET role) and session 401 vs 200 (DELETE sessions) on same stack with cross-worker visibility (requests routed via nginx round-robin to both gunicorn workers, SELECT verifies commit before batch, body SHA distinct 403 22B 387fe7... vs 401 25B 9df366...). Each must be full >=0.7 null 0.0. Localhost Flask dev (Werkzeug) replication of P-BODY/P-HEADER as sanity positive: same body/header states must still be 1.0 (if not, measurement system broken, -> MEASUREMENT_INVALID). BrowserGym/AgentLab positive if image available: same header/body comparands via 1280x720 browser GET (Playwright fetch) observed through BrowserGym HTTP layer; if image unavailable, mark NOT_TESTED, do not gate.
null_control: Null stability on production stack (mandatory): (N1-body) two independent batches N=20 each of GET /resource from same body STATE_A via nginx->gunicorn, no write between, jitter 50-150ms, concurrency 4 (4 parallel clients per batch via ThreadPool), expected full 0.0 with 95% bootstrap CI (B=1000) containing 0.0 and point <=0.05, and body-only 0.0 status-only 0.0 headers-only 0.0 headers-no-CLEN 0.0. (N1-header) two batches N=20 from same header STATE_A (31B constant) via production stack, same thresholds (tests header stability). (N-perm403) same-state 403 resampled N=20 vs N=20 via production stack, 0.0. (N-sess401) same-state 401 resampled, 0.0. All nulls run both sequential and concurrent (concurrent null measures CI non-degeneracy: with concurrency, fingerprint sets may gain variance if nginx adds Via/Connection differences; if fingerprints remain byte-identical, CI degenerate [0.0,0.0] declared deterministic and valid per measurement_validity). Localhost Flask dev null (sequential) as reference: body-A resampled 0.0. BrowserGym null if image available: same body resampled via browser fetch 0.0; else NOT_TESTED. Degenerate CI disclosure required (effective distinct N per state, set size). Any null >0.05 triggers falsification of production null stability; expected false-positive <0.05 per Director threshold.
measurement_validity: Fingerprint algorithm identity: hash(status || body_bytes || sorted_filtered_headers) with EXCLUDED_HEADERS={Date,Server,X-Request-Id} byte-identical to research/experiments/EXP-RUNTIME-35749360317/run_experiment.py:compute_fingerprint and parent EXP-RUNTIME-35697043449 (sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'), lowercased header keys sorted, values as-is). Code SHA logged; auditor recomputation must be 0 mismatches. Body-only vs header-only branches use same function; headers-no-CLEN computed by same function minus Content-Length key.

Server state snapshot per batch on production stack: body_config/content_variant and header_config read from SQLite (SELECT) and logged before each observation batch in batch_state_log.jsonl (27+ lines: 12 writes +15 verifies). POST /admin/set_body_variant and POST /admin/set_headers commit verified (WAL COMMIT) before 200; any SELECT mismatch aborts batch as MEASUREMENT_INVALID (COMMIT_NOT_VERIFIED).

Status identity verified per branch: body-only A/B/C all status=200 on every observation (40 per comparison, production via nginx); header-only A/E all 200; any non-200 where 200 required aborts that comparison as MEASUREMENT_INVALID (STATUS_MISMATCH) except classic 403/401 where 403/401 expected and verified separately.

Body byte-difference and Content-Length isolation: SHA-256(body_bytes) distinct across A vs C and A vs B on production stack, Content-Length header must equal body_len (proving no truncation or nginx chunked re-encoding mismatch) and differ 31 vs 70 vs 117 strictly increasing; non-CLEN filtered headers (Cache-Control, ETag, Vary, Set-Cookie) must be identical across body-only states (proving body-only not header-confounded); Date/Server/X-Request-Id excluded and logged; for header-only branch bodies 31B SHA identical and CLEN 31 identical, non-CLEN headers vary as programmed.

Header inclusion/exclusion and nginx normalization: Date varies per request but excluded, Server constant excluded, X-Request-Id absent excluded; Cache-Control, ETag, Set-Cookie, Vary INCLUDED but held constant on body-only and varied on header-only. B-HEADERS-ONLY and B-HEADERS-NO-CLEN computed with same algorithm. Nginx may lowercase headers or reorder; validation checks filtered_headers dict after lowercasing keys and sorting, not raw order. Multiple Set-Cookie handling: if nginx coalesces, log raw headers and compare sorted multi-value list; any unexpected variation in non-CLEN headers on body-only branch is validity failure (HEADER_DRIFT).

Gunicorn/nginx topology and concurrency: gunicorn workers=2 sync, bind 127.0.0.1:19860, nginx listen 127.0.0.1:19851 proxy_pass to upstream gunicorn (round-robin); nginx config and gunicorn command logged in provenance. Concurrency test uses ThreadPoolExecutor max_workers=4, 20 requests per state with 4 parallel; sequential baseline also measured (20 sequential) to isolate concurrency effect. Non-degenerate CI: bootstrap 95% CI B=1000 resampling fingerprint sets; degenerate [1.0,1.0] or [0.0,0.0] reported as deterministic when set size 1, not precision; width>0 reported as non-degenerate if fingerprints vary (e.g., Connection keep-alive differences if not excluded).

Distributed session replication: permission/session writes (UPDATE users SET role, DELETE sessions) committed to shared SQLite WAL file on same host; nginx round-robin ensures requests hit both gunicorn workers before verification batch (at least 10 requests per worker logged via X-Worker header or worker pid if injected). Redis alternative if available (if am1n3e/webarena-verified-shopping Redis detected, use Redis SET/DEL and verify via GET); at minimum SQLite WAL cross-worker visibility tested; per-worker batch_state_log verifies commit visible to both workers.

Seed and jitter: SEED=44 deterministic for request order, jitter 50-150ms uniform between observation bursts (not between concurrent parallel requests); N=20 per state nominal, effective distinct N reported per source; port discovery for gunicorn/nginx (19860/19851 or next free), fresh DB file per run, killed on exit; Flask/PyJWT/SQLite/Werkzeug/gunicorn/nginx versions recorded in provenance.

Artifact integrity and recomputation: raw_observations.jsonl (nominal 300 lines production stack: 60 body-only +40 header-only combined+isolations 60 +80 nulls = ~240-300) plus localhost replication (optional 60) with fields state, status, body_sha256, body_len, content_length_header, headers_filtered_json, headers_raw_json, headers_no_clen_json, fingerprint_full/status/body/headers/headers_no_clen, worker_id, timestamp, concurrency flag. batch_state_log.jsonl SHA-256 logged; recomputation of Jaccard distances by auditor must match within 0 mismatches; run_experiment.py SHA logged.

BrowserGym/AgentLab substrate (conditional): if Docker image am1n3e/webarena-verified-shopping or BrowserGym AgentLab (1280x720) available (docker image inspect succeeds), run header-only and body-only comparands via Playwright browser fetch through AgentLab HTTP observation layer, capturing same fingerprint triple; if image unavailable or pull fails, that substrate marked NOT_TESTED with reason IMAGE_UNAVAILABLE in validity_notes and result.json unresolved, and does NOT trigger MEASUREMENT_INVALID for gunicorn+nginx primary; CDN (Cloudflare/Fastly) not tested directly — nginx is local CDN proxy emulation, CDN GENERALIZATION marked unresolved.

Header folding/ordering/case test (exploratory but logged): send header_config variant with deliberately varied case (cache-control vs Cache-Control) and whitespace/order (Cache-Control: max-age=3600 vs " max-age=3600 " plus ETag order shuffled) via direct POST then GET; fingerprint must remain identical after sorted/lowercased normalization; if not, header folding robustness falsified but not gating primary discrimination (logged as C12).

Timing and commit visibility: body_config/header_config write committed before next observation batch; inter-batch delay 100ms plus SELECT verification; no concurrent writes during read batches; if commit not visible to second gunicorn worker within 500ms, retry SELECT and log worker divergence as validity note (DISTRIBUTED_DIVERGENCE).

Scope disclosure: CDN (Cloudflare paid-tier HIT/STALE, Vary, ETag) beyond nginx not tested; TLS/HTTP2 not tested (plain http 127.0.0.1 only); auth/session distributed replication tested only on single-host 2-worker gunicorn+nginx, not multi-host Redis cluster; BrowserGym 1280x720 browser DOM capture not tested beyond HTTP layer if image unavailable. All NOT_TESTED disclosed in validity_notes and report.
decision_rule: SUPPORTS (production generalization) requires ALL mandatory conditions on the production WSGI+nginx stack (measured via 127.0.0.1:19851 nginx -> gunicorn 2 workers, N=20 per state nominal, concurrency 4 for null and at least one body/header branch, fingerprint algorithm identical, EXCLUDED_HEADERS={Date,Server,X-Request-Id}): (C1_FULL_BODY_DRIFT_PROD) full-vector discrimination >0.5 (expected 1.0 deterministic) on primary same-status body-only A vs C (both 200, bodies 31B vs 117B SHA distinct, non-CLEN headers identical, Content-Length 31 vs 117). (C2_BODY_ONLY_SIGNAL_PROD) B-BODY-ONLY >0.5 (expected 1.0) on A vs C and on A vs B (70B vs 31B); B-HEADERS-NO-CLEN =0.0 on A vs C and A vs B (no independent header drift), while B-HEADERS-ONLY may be 1.0 solely via Content-Length. (C3_STATUS_ISOLATED_PROD) B-STATUS-ONLY =0.0 on A vs C and A vs B. (C4_FULL_EXCEEDS_STATUS_NONVACUOUS_PROD) full > B-STATUS-ONLY strictly on A vs C (e.g., 1.0 > 0.0, complement to header-only). (C5_NULL_NO_FALSE_POSITIVE_PROD) null N1-body (same body A resampled, two independent N=20 batches via production stack, concurrent) full =0.0 with 95% bootstrap CI containing 0.0 and point <=0.05 and B-STATUS-ONLY=0.0 B-BODY-ONLY=0.0 on null; same for N1-header (same header A resampled) and classic nulls (same-state 403 resampled, same-state 401 resampled) each 0.0 <=0.05. (C6_CONTENT_LENGTH_VARIES_AND_HEADERS_CONSTANT_PROD) Content-Length differs proportional to body_len (31 !=70 !=117) and body SHA distinct, while non-CLEN filtered headers identical across A/B/C and Content-Length==body_len on each observation. (C7_WRITABLE_PERMISSION_PROD) writable permission controls full >=0.7: (a) permission-filtered body reader 200 vs admin 200 (A vs C) >=0.7 (auto if C1 1.0) and (b) classic escalation 403 vs 200 via UPDATE users SET role on production stack with cross-worker commit, full >=0.7 with body SHA distinct status 403 vs 200 verified and its null 0.0. (C8_WRITABLE_SESSION_PROD) writable session invalidation 401 vs 200 via DELETE sessions on production stack with cross-worker commit, full >=0.7 status 401 vs 200 verified and null 0.0. (C9_HEADER_ONLY_PROD) header-only full >0.5 (expected 1.0) and headers-only >0.5 on A vs E (bodies 31B identical SHA same, CLEN 31 identical, status 200 vs 200) with B-BODY-ONLY=0.0 B-STATUS-ONLY=0.0 on same comparison; per-isolation Cache-Control only, ETag only, Set-Cookie only each full 1.0 headers-only 1.0 status 0.0 body 0.0. (C10_CLEN_IDENTITY_HEADER_ONLY_PROD) Content-Length identical (31==31) and body SHA identical across header-only A vs E and each isolation, proving header-only not body-confounded. All C1-C10 must pass for SUPPORTS. If any fails where validity checks passed -> FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING for production generalization (bounded to gunicorn+nginx localhost, 127.0.0.1, Flask 3.1.3 HS256, 2 workers, nginx reverse proxy). If infrastructure prevents verification (gunicorn/nginx binary missing, port bind fails, COMMIT_NOT_VERIFIED, STATUS_MISMATCH, BODY_NOT_DISTINCT, HEADER_DRIFT outside included set, image unavailable for BrowserGym) -> MEASUREMENT_INVALID with category and retryability. Exploratory (not gating SUPPORTS but reported): (E1 CI_NONDEGENERATE) bootstrap CI width >0 measured under concurrency; expected degenerate if fingerprint deterministic, disclosed as deterministic not precision; (E2 HEADER_FOLDING) case/whitespace/order normalization holds; (E3 DISTRIBUTED_VISIBILITY) permission/session commit visible to both workers within 500ms; (E4 BROWSERGYM) BrowserGym HTTP-layer discrimination if image available (else NOT_TESTED).
product_consequence_positive: C-MEAS-VALID ceiling expands from localhost Flask dev (Werkzeug) EXPERIMENTAL to production-like WSGI (gunicorn) + nginx reverse proxy EXPERIMENTAL with non-vacuous body-only and header-only discrimination both validated on same stack (full 1.0 >0.5, body/status isolation 0.0, null <0.05, writable >=0.7) under concurrency and cross-worker commit visibility. This removes the single largest blocking assumption identified in portfolio assessment (42 localhost streak, tunnel_flag true, C-MEAS-VALID not VALIDATED): freshness/delta-repair claims beyond localhost no longer rest on untested header folding/ordering, nginx buffering, WSGI worker isolation or SQLite WAL cross-worker visibility. Graph C-DELTA-REPAIR (4 BLOCKED) and Physics beyond-memory tests can now proceed with trusted substrate for both content-only (200 vs 200 body varies) and metadata-only (200 vs 200 header varies) drift on production-like middleware; Graph can calibrate freshness policies with body vs header signal strength gradient now measured (both 1.0 at tested magnitudes, ordering still at ceiling) and can test distributed C-FRESHNESS C1 TN fix with Redis/sticky routing using this substrate. No promotion to VALIDATED or PRODUCT_CORE yet: still bounded to localhost-hosted gunicorn+nginx (no paid-tier CDN Cloudflare HIT/SWR/SIE, no TLS/HTTP2, no multi-host Redis cluster, no BrowserGym 1280x720 DOM capture if image unavailable, degenerate CI effective N=1, value magnitudes 31/70/117 and 3 header variants only). Next step is CDN HIT/SWR/SIE 960/960 analogue on real CDN or full BrowserGym WebArena family hold-out.
product_consequence_negative: C-MEAS-VALID production generalization falsified: HTTP fingerprint substrate that was deterministic 1.0/0.0 on localhost Flask dev fails on production WSGI+nginx (gunicorn workers, nginx header folding/ordering/whitespace/case, concurrency, cross-worker SQLite WAL) for at least one mandatory branch: either same-status body-only (full <=0.5 or status !=0.0 or headers-no-CLEN !=0.0 or CLEN not varying), or header-only (full <=0.5 or body/status !=0.0 or CLEN not identical), or null FP>0.05, or writable permission/session <0.7 or not visible cross-worker. This proves localhost determinism does not transfer to production middleware; nginx buffering, header normalization, worker isolation or SQLite WAL visibility breaks discrimination or isolation. Direct product consequence: C-FRESHNESS and C-DELTA-REPAIR cannot trust HTTP fingerprint for freshness guards or delta repair on production WSGI/nginx/CDN; freshness distributed TN=0.667 failure remains blocked and requires alternative substrate (explicit body diff, DOM observation, Redis shared session, or CDN-aware header handling) or server-side header/body canonicalization before any production or distributed testing. Negative is high-information: it bounds the substrate to Flask dev server only, prevents false trust in production freshness guards, and forces redesign (header canonicalization, Content-Length handling, worker-shared state) before scaling; Graph must not tune freshness on this substrate until fixed, and Physics beyond-memory tests must use different observation layer.
estimated_cost: Medium: single-host gunicorn (2 workers) + nginx reverse proxy (config generation, no paid CDN), plus localhost Flask dev sanity control, same Flask 3.1.3 + PyJWT already installed; gunicorn pip install (~1 min), nginx binary (apt or docker nginx:alpine, pull if needed <2 min), 240-300 observations via nginx (body-only 60 + header-only 60 + nulls 80 + classic 40) x2 topologies (sequential + concurrent 4) ~10-12 min sequential plus nginx/gunicorn start/stop, optional BrowserGym image pull (only if intel dependency am1n3e/webarena-verified-shopping / AgentLab available, else skip and mark NOT_TESTED); total wall-clock ~15-20 min, deterministic, no external paid services, no large browser corpus.
expected_information_gain: Very high and discriminating: first production-middleware test of the HTTP fingerprint substrate after 42 localhost experiments (tunnel_flag true); directly tests the systemic enabler that blocks Graph C-DELTA-REPAIR (4 BLOCKED) and limits Physics/Product claims to localhost mocks per Global Research Director portfolio assessment. Positive would close the localhost->production promotion gap (header folding, WSGI concurrency, distributed session replication non-degenerate CI) and unblock downstream freshness distributed replication and BrowserGym family hold-out. Negative is equally decisive: it falsifies production generalization and forces substrate redesign before any distributed freshness or delta repair can be trusted, preventing false product promotion. Either outcome changes the Codex claim ceiling from degenerate CI localhost to production-evaluated (non-degenerate where concurrency exposes variance) and resolves the Director's binding question, which no further localhost body/header magnitude variant can address (all prior variants hit ceiling 1.0, no gradient).
